description: Surface Water Network is a Python package for turning mapped stream lines into a connected network. It reads line geometries from a shapefile or PostGIS source, identifies segments, headwaters, outlets and diversions, and can export network objects and geospatial files. An optional interface supports MODFLOW-related workflows. Geography and time depend on the supplied river-line dataset; the package itself has no fixed basin or observation period. Its source is free under BSD-3-Clause and the README gives installation dependencies, tests and a worked stream-network example. The example uses 304 segments, but that is illustrative, not product coverage. A key limit is that a geometrically connected river network does not by itself specify discharge, routing parameters or water quality. It can prepare topology for catchment, groundwater-surface-water and flood simulations. The catalogue's model-raven is one hydrological model that may use basin network information, although this specific package-to-model link was not run. No source map or model archive was downloaded.
